cards.note: Due to Alaska’s very cold climate; agricultural fields are mainly found in the south of the state, mostly in the Matanuska Valley and Kenai Peninsula.

The Alaskan towns in the Alexander Archipelago, on the British Columbia border have a unique look. Tall mountains with lush green forests can be seen in the background, with the majority of buildings made of wood. In addition, Generation 2 coverage is often overcast and misty.

NOTE: Coastal areas of Oregon and Washington can have a similar appearance in terms of landscape and foliage.

The Alaskan towns in the Alexander Archipelago, on the British Columbia border have a unique look. Tall mountains with lush green forests can be seen in the background, with the majority of buildings made of wood.

NOTE: Coastal areas of Oregon and Washington can have a similar appearance in terms of landscape and foliage.

The Denali highway (8), stretching from Cantwell to Paxson in central Alaska, is a mostly gravel highway in the ‘Alaska’ mountain range. This road runs generally east to west, is covered in the generation 2 camera, and was taken in late summer, so wildflowers and green shrubby plants are common.

Juneau, Alaska’s Capital city, is the largest settlement in the Alaskan panhandle. Therefore, it is much more ‘built up’ than other towns in this area. The city is surrounded by heavily forested mountains and hills.

The Kenai peninsula can be recognized by its massive amount of fireweed along the roads. Most of the coverage is Gen 3 Autumn. Along AK-1 you will often see a bay to the west with mountains on the other side.
The North end of the Dalton Highway (11) features a flat and snowy landscape and an overcast sky. A small ridge of hills can be seen to the west of the highway in certain spots.
Prudhoe Bay, the northernmost town in America covered by street view, can be recognized by cold, dead landscape, overcast clouds and lack of tall buildings. A second Google car can sometimes be seen.

The Steese Highway (6) is a gravel highway that goes from Fairbanks to the town of ‘Central.’ Similar to the Denali highway, this road runs generally east to west and is covered in generation 2. The difference, however, is that the mountains along this road are noticeably lower than the ones adjacent to the Denali Highway.

cards.a: Alaska - Landscape - Suburban Area with Mountains
cards.note: Suburban areas around Anchorage feature wide roads, commercial districts, and sometimes heavy traffic. Mountains can commonly be seen in the distance.

cards.a: Alaska - Landscape - Suburban Area without Mountains
cards.note: Suburban areas around Anchorage feature wide roads, commercial districts, and sometimes heavy traffic. Compared to Anchorage, the landscape is flatter.
Most of interior and northern Alaska lies in subarctic or tundra climate zones. These areas feature relatively low amounts of forest undergrowth and shorter trees.
The only two major urban areas in Alaska are Anchorage and Fairbanks.
Afono Bay is the only Bay with coverage that is opened towards straight North. Note that Fagasa Bay is opened towards Northwest, while Vatia Bay is opened towards Northeast.

Behold: The Camel Rock. Two little peaks reaching into the ocean.

It is marked as a POI on Google Maps.

cards.a: American Samoa - Landscape - East of Summit 001 - Overcast
cards.note:
This road crosses the district border on the 001. It is characterized through the unique angle and the mountains in the north. Often you can see a unique summit in the west. The driving direction is eastwards.

There is a stretch of the 001 with a similar angle near Malaeimi, but it has a clearly visible valley in the North which is not found on this road.

The road can further be divided as it is overcast in the Western District and sunny in the Eastern District.

cards.a: American Samoa - Landscape - East of Summit 001 - Sunny
cards.note:
This road crosses the district border on the 001. It is characterized through the unique angle and the mountains in the north. Often you can see a unique summit in the west. The driving direction is eastwards.

There is a stretch of the 001 with a similar angle near Malaeimi, but it has a clearly visible valley in the North which is not found on this road.

The road can further be divided as it is overcast in the Western District and sunny in the Eastern District.

cards.a: American Samoa - Landscape - Eastern South Coast Road
cards.note:
This long stretch of road (which is probably further regionguessable) is easily recognizable because it has a South Coast and the Car Drives westward (unlike the Western Coastal Road). That means that when you pan onto the back of the truck, the water will be to your right.

There is one annoying exception, around the POI 'Amouli Beach Fales' east of the town Amouli.
Afono Bay is the only Bay with coverage that is opened towards Northwest. Note that Afono is opened towards North proper, while Vatia Bay is opened towards Northeast.

cards.a: American Samoa - Landscape - Manu'a - North Coast road (paved)
cards.note: On Manu'a/Olosega (which have a unique car), there are two covered roads with North coast: The roads east and west of the famous bridge. They can easily be differentiated, because the Olosega (east) road is unpaved, while the Manu'a (west) road has concrete pavement.

cards.a: American Samoa - Landscape - Manu'a - North Coast road (unpaved)
cards.note: On Manu'a/Olosega (which have a unique car), there are two covered roads with North coast: The roads east and west of the famous bridge. They can easily be differentiated, because the Olosega (east) road is unpaved, while the Manu'a (west) road has concrete pavement.

The town Ofu on Manu'a has a West Coast. This road can be distinguished from the West Coast of Olosega, because:

  • It is entirely paved (unlike the town Olosega)
  • It has no Mountain in the North (unlike the paved road north of Olosega).

cards.a: American Samoa - Landscape - Pago Pago Harbour
cards.note: The roads alonog the Pago Pago Harbour are recognizable because they're generally very urban (for American Samoa), and you can often see the harbour when it isn't blocked by buildings.
Faleasao is a little town on Tau (and thus has the Tau car). It has a coast in the North and is otherwise surrounded by mountains. Together with the Tau car, it is unique.

The Rte 018 in Tafuna is urban and uniquely shows this mountain in the North. The alignment is generally North-South. The road has double yellow lines (not that common in AS) and a power line in the East. The driving direction is to the North.

Make sure that parts of the Rte 001 can look similar with a similar road angle. To confirm it's the Rte 018, you can pan exactly North. If you look at the mountain, it's the Rte 018, otherwise it's not.

cards.a: American Samoa - Landscape - Tutuila East Coast
cards.note: This is the only part of Tutuila where you can see Coast on the east, without other parts of Tutuila visible. You will often see Aunu'u in the Southeast.
Vatia Bay is the only Bay with coverage that is opened towards Northeast. Note that Fagasa Bay is opened towards Northwest, while Afono Bay is opened towards North proper.

cards.a: American Samoa - Landscape - Western South Coast Road
cards.note:
This road is easily recognizable because it has a South Coast and the Car drives eastward (unlike the Eastern Coastal Road). That means that when you pan onto the back of the truck, the water will be to your left.

On the eastern south coast road, there is a tiny part that also drives eastward for some reason, which can be baity.
Semi-coastal grass hills are seen in southern Buenos Aires, especially northeast of Bahía Blanca.
In the Chaco and Formosa provinces, you will often see sandy soil with an abundance of vegetation; mainly low trees and bushes.
Comodoro Rivadavia is built on the slopes of Chenque hill, making the city recognisable.
These mountains are typically found west of Córdoba.
Flat and barren landscapes like this are typically found in central southern Argentina.
Grassland with a few separated tree plantations is generally found in this area.
The RP1 in Neuquen has dark, cloudy coverage. It is a dark red dirt road and thus resembles Mars. There is some spill onto the RP7 in the North and the RP10 in the South.
If you see this kind of vegetation with flat grass and a low number of bushes, you are almost certainly in the state of Tierra del Fuego or southeastern Santa Cruz.
Far western Argentina typically features a mountainous landscape.
These red mountains are unique to the RN68 valley in southern Salta.
Red soil is typically found in the Misiones province.
The western part of the RN65 in western Tucumán can easily be recognized by this bendy unpaved road up in the mountains.

cards.a: Argentina - Landscape - Road of Death - Cloudy
cards.note: The western part of the RN65 in western Tucumán can easily be recognized by this bendy unpaved road up in the mountains with its western part up in the clouds.
Salt pans in Argentina are typically found in Jujuy.
Roads with reddish pavement lined with long Argentine needle-grass are common in San Luis.

cards.a: Argentina - Landscape - Small Lakes and Ponds
cards.note: Small lakes near the road are occasionally seen in the province of Buenos Aires.
Red soil with a barren landscape and mountain ranges, can often be seen on the RN76 in Parque Nacional Talampaya in western La Rioja.
These snowy mountains to the north can only be found in Ushuaia.

cards.a: Argentina - Landscape - Villa Dique Florentino Ameghino
cards.note: Villa Dique Florentino Ameghino in northeastern Chubut is surrounded by these rock formations.

cards.a: Argentina - Landscape - Villa Dique Florentino Ameghino Dam
cards.note: This unique dam with the rock formations typical for Villa Dique Florentino Ameghino can be found west of the town.
These volcanic rocks in Generation 4 coverage can only be found on the RP43 south of Antofagasta de la Sierra in northwestern Catamarca.
Alice Springs, an isolated town in the southern part of the Northern Territory, features distinct orange rocks that can be seen in the distance or at the end of roads.
The northern QLD city of Cairns is distinct due to its tropical vegetation and big green mountains around the city.
The vegetation in the area surrounding Darwin is extremely distinct. It features dark red soil, as well as rich green grass and trees. The tree trunks are typically black.

cards.a: Australia - Landscape - Eastern South Australia Landscape
cards.note:
The dry area east of Adelaide and into northwestern Victoria has quite dry vegetation and is made up of shrubs and wide cronwed eucalyptus. In addition, the soil is sandy with a white tint.

Western South Australia has a similar landscape, but with orangish soil.

Lush green or golden fields can be found in this band from the south of the Yorke Peninsula to Echuca. In the SA side, the landscape should be drier than the Victorian side and more wide crowned eucalyptus can be seen. On the Victorian side, the trees generally have more leaves and are taller.

cards.a: Australia - Landscape - Inland New South Wales Landscape
cards.note: The landscape in inland NSW is mostly flat, and the soil gets redder the more inland you go. Vegetation consists of mostly dry pale-green shrubs. Further east and on the Queensland and Victorian borders, the climate gets more temperate but is still quite dry and more eucalyptus trees can be seen, with the soil transitioning into a more sandy colour as well as more hills being visible.

Kangaroo Island in South Australia tends to have a distinct look. The vegetation mostly consists of bushes and low, stubby eucalyptus trees with puffy clusters of leaves. The orange soil colour is reminiscent of Western Australia.

In addition, the island only has Generation 2 and Generation 4 coverage, with Generation 2 being most common.

cards.a: Australia - Landscape - Mount Gambier Tree Plantations
cards.note: The area around Mount Gambier, SA features white soil and extensive pine tree plantations, making it recognisable.
Coastal northern Queensland is very tropical. Typical vegetation consists of palm trees and dark green vegetation.

The Nullarbor Highway (Latin for “no tree”) can be easily recognized thanks to the flatness, overall grey look and very low vegetation.

NOTE: Use the road angle or road lines to determine whether you are on the WA or SA side.
Western Australia, and especially the Perth area, is known for its reddish-orange soil.

cards.a: Australia - Landscape - Stuart Highway with Blue Car
cards.note: The Stuart Highway from Alice Springs to around Pimba, SA can be easily recognized by its bright orange dirt, short trees and blue car Generation 4.

Tasmania has a cool temperate climate which is uncommon in the rest of Australia and is comparable to central-southern Chile or New Zealand. Typical landscape consists of green rolling hills that can look dry in winter coverage. Eucalyptus trees can be seen on the side of roads and on hills in the distance. Rural Tasmania is also quite hilly with dense eucalyptus forests making up the landscape.
Termite mounds can sometimes be seen in the Northern Territory and rarely northern WA and QLD. They appear as brown, spiky formations rising out of the ground.
The area around Tom Price can be recognized by its red soil and rocky hills.

cards.a: Australia - Landscape - Western South Australia Landscape
cards.note:
The area around Warramboo in SA to Madura in WA has a unique landscape. Vegetation is quite dry and is made up of shrubs and wide crowned eucalyptus. In addition, the soil is sandy with a slight orange tint.

The dry area east of Adelaide and into northwestern Victoria has a similar landscape, with the same vegetation but usually with whiter soil.

Acre has a unique landscape of small grass hills and sparsely growing trees. The roads often do not cut around the hills like in most of Brazil, but ride the hills instead. A similar landscape can also be seen near Maraba in the state of Pará.

The Amazon is a dense rainforest that compromises 40% of Brazil's total area. Not many roads are within it, but those that are, mostly go through either biodiverse forest or grassy hills with sparse trees.

The Amazonas 319 has a very lush, bright green and tropical landscape, as it cuts through the Amazon rainforest. The road is flat and mostly unpaved, featuring bright orange soil. However, closer to Manaus the road becomes paved. There are wooden or ladder poles alongside the entire stretch. It is covered by the blue Generation 4 car.

The Pará section of the 163 is often hilly, curvy, dry, and sometimes hazy. It has a wide range of amazonian vegetation. The road is frequently trafficked, usually by transportation trucks. It is covered by the blue Generation 4 car.
This road can be recognized by the Amazonian looking trees and the NW/SE angle. It always has Gen 4 and an exposed, blue car front.
This wide dirt road has Amazonian trees and a blurred car. You will not find other cars on the road. It's the only East-to-West angle road in that area.
This road looks like an Amazonian road with the trees and dense rainforest. It runs east-west, slightly to the south. The road looks like its stained with mud

cards.a: Brazil - Landscape - BR319, North of Porto Velho
cards.note: This road is characterized by it's Amazonian look and the SW-NE road angle. Some sections of this road are overcast and/or showcase a flat landscape.
Northeastern Brazil can be identified by its dry soil, shrubs and succulents (the Caatinga landscape).

cards.a: Brazil - Landscape - Caatinga landscape - rain coverage
cards.note: Northeastern Brazil can be identified by its dry soil, shrubs and succulents (the Caatinga landscape). In rainy season coverage, the shrubs are still recognizable, but can be deceptively green.

This road in eastern Santa Catarina is characterized by its windyness and by the steep mountains and cliffs along its side. It can feel like your driving with the clouds. The road goes through Corvo Branco which is a famous tourist attraction.
This road east of Fortaleza is characterized by its unique pavement and the sanddunes along the road.
Espírito Santo, and the surrounding areas, often have large mountains with exposed rock.
Coastal regions in Rio Grande do Sul are recognisable due to being a rare flat wetland, which is uncommon in Brazil.

cards.a: Brazil - Landscape - Landbridge in Rio Grande do Sul
cards.note: Recognizable by the swamp-like landscape, the pine trees along the road and the Lagoon It runs at a SE-NW angle.
Ilha de Fernando de Noronha is similar in vegetation to NE-Brazil and has large exposed rocks.

cards.a: Brazil - Landscape - North of Uiramuta road
cards.note: This very unique looking road features rolling hills, which is unusual for the rather flat Roraima. It is a windy dirt road and despite being green, it lacks trees. What seperates this from the road south of Uiramuta is that it's more skinny and steeper.

cards.a: Brazil - Landscape - Rio Grande do Sul Landscape
cards.note: The landscape in Rio Grande do Sul can be hilly or flat with lush, green fields. Southern areas can have some resemblance to Uruguay.

The 364 through Acre is very recognisable due to the rollercoaster-like landscape and road: the road uniquely rides the hills rather than snaking around them. There is usually no traffic, and is covered mostly by Generation 3 with an antenna.

Rural locations in Roraima are mostly open grassy plains with large, distant mountains in the background. Occasionally, you are on roads within the mountains. Furthermore, the grass in Roraima is distinctly thin, and grows in bunches.

Serra do Mar is a high mountain range that runs close to the coast from Parana to Northern RGDS.

If you have a high altitude road going on the mountains, instead of in the valleys, you're likely here.

This very unique looking road features rolling hills, which is unusual for the rather flat Roraima. It is a windy dirt road and despite being green, it lacks trees. What seperates this from the road south of Uiramuta is that it's less skinny and less steep.
Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro and Espírito Santo often have rolling grassy hills.
A very swampy road (PA-154) can be found Northwest of Belém. Notably, there are very few trees, and the soil is very red.
This beautiful road west of Cascavel and South of Toledo, by the PR-585 is characterized by the uneven red stone pavement and the corn plantation next to it.
The A-31 can be recognised by its high altitude, with a steep drop into a valley to the north. The road also has Gen 3 sunset coverage.

After crossing the Lluta River at Poconchile, the Ruta 11 continues out of the valley and up into the mountains. The road is all newly paved (except for a few small segments with ongoing construction) and is generally quite wide. This section of Ruta 11 features:

  • Many concrete barriers (which are often painted yellow), double guardrails, and roadside drainage ways.
  • Maroon-colored asphalt in some places.
  • Mountains are made of light reddish sand with occasional exposed rock. Rounded protrusions are also common

The landscape is bare of vegetation until around Zapahuira, east of which the landscape becomes open and covered with small green bushes.

cards.a: Chile - Landscape - A11 - Lluta River Valley
cards.note: Along the Lluta River, the Ruta 11 passes through a wide valley lined by sloping, sandy mountains that often feature distinctly round rock protrusions. The valley is home to a large amount of agriculture relative to other parts of the Atacama Desert. You’ll often see sizable green fields lined by bushes, trees, or wooden fences, as well as bunches of planted Mexican fan palms. A railroad track also follows the Lluta River on both sides, so if you’re in a green valley next to both a river and a railroad, you’re almost certainly on Ruta 11.

After crossing the Lluta River at Poconchile, the Ruta 11 continues out of the valley and up into the mountains. The road is all newly paved (except for a few small segments with ongoing construction) and is generally quite wide. The landscape is bare of vegetation until around Zapahuira, east of which the landscape becomes open and covered with small green bushes.

cards.a: Chile - Landscape - Alto Bio Bio National Reserve
cards.note: A vast, mostly treeless landscape combined with triple yellow lines are seen in Alto Bio Bio National Reserve. While the reserve may look dry, there is a distinct cold and high altitude feel.

cards.a: Chile - Landscape - Alto Bio Bio National Reserve - Monkey Puzzle Trees
cards.note: A vast, mostly treeless landscape combined with triple yellow lines are seen in Alto Bio Bio National Reserve. While the reserve may look dry, there is a distinct cold and high altitude feel. Monkey puzzles are also seen toward the east.

cards.a: Chile - Landscape - Alto Loa National Reserve
cards.note: Alto Loa National Reserve can be recognized by the vast, open landscape, followed by salt pans leading up to snow-capped volcanoes. The reserve does not have any paved roads.
A rockier, and more uneven ridge can be seen in Antofagasta.

The province of Arica y Parinacota can be recognized by the smooth, sandy mountains that may look slightly eroded, or have bulbous formations. Valleys are also common, which are rarely seen in other parts of Chile.
A slight, sandy ridge with a gradual incline can be seen in Arica.

The Atacama is an extremely arid desert covering the northern third of Chile. Some parts of it experience the lowest rainfall on the planet. As a result, many locations in this desert are almost completely devoid of any vegetation: you will often just see sand and bare rock without any plants in sight anywhere.

NOTE: The Atacama Desert also covers parts of southern Peru, western Bolivia and northwestern Argentina.
These rocky, uneven mountains are most commonly seen in Atacama and northern Coquimbo.

This brownish red soil can sometimes be seen in Atacama province.

NOTE: This is most reliable in Generation 3. This soil can be seen in other provinces in Generation 4.

A rolling, agricultural landscape, comparable to New Zealand, can be seen on Isla Grande de Chiloé.

NOTE: Similar looking landscapes exist in some other parts of the country, but usually more level.
The region around Santiago can be recognized by its semi-arid climate, having dry hills and scattered vegetation.
Eucalyptus plantations combined with a somewhat dry climate are a good indicator that you are in southwestern Valparaíso.
A large, towering ridge can be seen in Iquique.

East of Putre, Ruta 11 enters Lauca National Park which has a flatter landscape, with tall snow-capped mountains in the background, and features unique Andean Plateau vegetation like Peruvian feather grass and the recognizable cushion plant yareta (Azorella compacta). You can also find Chilean bollards lining the road, which are extremely rare.

Lauca can look very similar to other areas in the east Andes of northern Chile, but it’s recognizable for the iconic Volcán Parinacota, a tall snow-capped volcano that stands alone and away from other mountain ridges. It’s visible from basically every location in the park, though it can be shrouded by clouds.

cards.a: Chile - Landscape - Llanos de Challe National Park
cards.note: Llanos de Challe National Park can be recognized by the brown coloured dirt on the roadside, patches of light sand, juniper plants, and dark coloured mountains. The sky is overcast in most of the coverage.

cards.a: Chile - Landscape - Los Flamencos National Reserve
cards.note: Smooth mountains with a reddish tint are seen in Los Flamencos National Reserve. Salt pans are also a common sight. The reserve uses triple yellow lines.

cards.a: Chile - Landscape - Los FLamencos National Reserve - Short Dashes
cards.note: Smooth mountains with a reddish tint are seen in Los Flamencos National Reserve. Salt pans are also a common sight. The reserve uses triple yellow lines, with short dashes in the west.
Lush green valleys, with rocky mountains and often overcast coverage, can be seen in southern Los Lagos and northern Aysén.
Compared to the area around Santiago, the Maule province has a similar look. However, it has a Mediterranean climate, and is generally greener.
Narrow roads with trees on both sides can commonly be seen in the provinces of Bio Bio and Araucania.

cards.a: Chile - Landscape - Nevado Tres Cruces National Park
cards.note: In the west, Nevado Tres Cruces National Park can be recognized by the vast, open landscape, followed by salt pans leading up to a line of mountains. The sand has a reddish tint.

cards.a: Chile - Landscape - Nevado Tres Cruces National Park - Snow
cards.note: In the east of this park, the Google Car drives up a mountain pass with views of lightly snow-capped volcanoes and snow on the side of the road. The roads in the National Park are paved.
The northern section of Pampa del Tamarugal National Reserve can be recognized by the Tamarugo trees lining the road. The road itself is mediocre quality, and in a consistent north-west direction.

cards.a: Chile - Landscape - Pan de Azucar National Park
cards.note: Pan de Azucar National Park can be recognized by the brown coloured dirt on the roadside, patches of light sand, little vegetation, and dark coloured mountains. The sky is overcast in most of the coverage
Puyehue National Park can be recognized by the dense vegetation surrounding the road. The pavement itself has triple yellow lines, and tar snakes are frequently seen.

cards.a: Chile - Landscape - Puyehue National Park - Dead Trees
cards.note: Puyehue National Park can be recognized by the dense vegetation surrounding the road. The pavement itself has triple yellow lines, and tar snakes are frequently seen. In the east, many dead trees can be seen with a lack of leaves.

Ruta 1 is a coastal road that is easily recognized by the wall of mountains to the east, and the Pacific Ocean to the west. This image shows the various weather conditions faced on the road to help you make closer guesses.
Ruta 181 leading up to Alto Bio Bio National Reserve has triple yellow lines, looks similar to the reserve but with more vegetation.

Part of Ruta 41 is located in a valley, with snowy mountains seen in the distance. Many trees and vineyards can commonly be seen toward the west. Triple white lines west of the middle between Balala and Miraflores.

Part of Ruta 41 is located in a valley, with snowy mountains seen in the distance. Many trees and vineyards can commonly be seen toward the west. Triple yellow lines east of the middle between Balala and Miraflores.
O’Higgins can be recognized by the large mountains to the east, often casting a shadow over the town. To the west, snow-capped mountains are seen further in the distance.

cards.a: Colombia - Landscape - Deep grey & stony soil in Gen 3
cards.note: This type of soil can be found in towns near the pacific coast.

cards.a: Colombia - Landscape - East of Andes Landscape
cards.note:
East of the Andes lies a vast lowland called Llanos. It is characterised by open tropical grasslands, savannas with scattered trees, small areas of forest and seasonal flooding.

Since it's to the east of the Andes, you may see mountains in the west, but never in the east.
This striking cone-shaped mountain can often be seen from the surrounding area of Guatape.
The only road in Guaviare goes from to Guaviare (city), and continues south up until Vda. El Trueno. It can be recognized by the orange-looking dust on the road.
This landscape is typical of the far Northern province of La Guajira: extreme dryness, low vegetation and occasional cacti.
The Northern part of the country is characterised by white, sandy soil and an arid landscape.

Paramos refers to alpine tundra ecosystems located in the mountains. These kinds of regions are easy to guess by how little vegetation grows here. The best clue is these odd looking pants. ( giant rosette plants ).

Note by MB: In my experience, this appears most commonly south of Bogota, still in the capital district.

In southern Colombia, around the city of Pasto, there are hilly fields that are unique in that they are bordered by hedges. The hedges are very thick and form very distinctive lines on the hills. It almost gives off a “British” vibe. If you are sure that it is Colombia, this is a very good meta, but such fields with hedges also occur in Ecuador.

!! In very rare cases, such hedges on hills can also occur in other parts of Colombia. !!
Santa Rosalia is the only town covered in Vichada. So if you see red/orange dirt in an urban Gen 4 loc, you should go there.

cards.a: Colombia - Landscape - Swamp Road + Extremely Sunny
cards.note: If you see a swamp road with extremely sunny coverage, you're probably on the 74 in Sucre.
The 74, the 78 and a few other roads more north have very swampy parts, you can see on the map where these are by zooming.

cards.a: Colombia - Landscape - Unique Road - 78 west of Pailitas
cards.note: This road is characterised by low clouds and a towering mountain in the east.

cards.a: Colombia - Landscape - Unique Road - Ruta 90 Landbridge
cards.note:
You can recognise the narrow Ruta 90 landbridge between Barranquilla and Cienaga thanks to the dashed yellow lines and shallow bodies of water next to the road. Open ocean can often be seen to the north.

NOTE: In the older Generation 3 coverage, you will also see tall mountains in the distance.

cards.a: Colombia - Landscape - Unique Road - Uribia to Puerto Boliviar
cards.note: You can often recognise the Uribia-Puerto Bolivar road because of La Guajira landscape (extreme dryness, low vegetation and occasional cacti), the straightness and the train track always present to the East.
Vichada is characterize by hazy Gen 4 coverage and Red Dirt.

Rural roads surrounded by hedges blocking the view, reminiscent of the British Isles, are primarily found in the northwest, particularly in Normandy.

NOTE: Hedges by themselves are not sufficient for recognizing this area and are common all over France.

The French Riviera (Cote d'Azur) will mirror many characteristics of Monaco. Rich areas with planted palms and light coloured multi story buildings with wide balconies are good indications you’re in this area, with the rest of the southern coast and Corsican Bastia sharing similar vibes.

La Beauce is one of the flattest regions of France, located South of Paris.

Apart from the flatness of the area, the important thing to notice about the fields in the Beauce region is that they are industrialized. You will not see hedges around the fields like you could see in the West of France. So, if you see very flat and industrialized fields with potatoes or cereals, you can be in this area. Still, the Paris hedge remains good because there are many fields North and East of Paris (but you will never get a 5K by guessing Paris out of fields).
The tallest mountains are found in the southeast and on the Spanish border.
The German Alps is the most mountainous region in Germany, it is mostly concentrated on the Austrian Border.
The North and especially Northwest of Germany is very flat.
Central Germany is hilly.
The flat plains southeast of Regensburg can be recognised by the slight ridge often visible to the northeast. The plains themselves are flat, and quite agricultural.

The shrub and sand covered hills are unique to the island of Sylt. And like the rest of the North Frisian Islands, rock walls, brick houses, and thatched roofs are common.

NOTE: Some parts of Sylt look more generic, but still very flat.

The Island of Maui sits southeast of Molokaʻi. In the centre of the island, you will find somewhat flat grasslands. It has the very recognizable West Maui Mountains to the west, and Haleakala to the east.

The coastal areas of the island of Hawai’i are where most of the towns and built-up areas on the island are located. These areas are typically more lush and have more trees and fern plants than the interior.

Note by MB: There is a similar road, the Hana Highway on Maui, which is more narrow and has narrower shoulders than the typical road on Hawai'i.
Towards the coasts of the island of Lānaʻi, hills dotted with dry grass and shrubby vegetation are commonly seen. These areas are very rural with few buildings.
Coastal areas of Maui are noticeably lush and green. Banana plants, palm trees, and views of the mountains are all common.

Rather flat and wide volcano, making it's shape quite unique.

As the name suggests, it's found in the East of Moloka'i island.
Rural roads going through forests within a flat landscape are commonly found south of the city of Hilo, on the island of Hawaiʻi.
The area near Kula is at the foot of Haleakala and often looks over the rest of the island.

The Hana Highway runs along the coast of Maui and is narrow and lush in the North.

Note by MB: Note that unlike in the picture, Hana Highway also has center lines on some parts. That creates a possible toss-up with Hawai'i island. However, Hana Highway is more narrow and has very narrow shoulders, unlike most roads on Hawai'i.

The Hana Highway runs along the coast of Maui and is narrow. In the south, the landscape is fairly open and you can often see the southern coast, as no trees are in the way.

Note by MB: Note that unlike in the picture, Hana Highway also has center lines on some parts. That creates a possible toss-up with Hawai'i island. However, Hana Highway is more narrow and has very narrow shoulders, unlike most roads on Hawai'i.

The infamous 'Hawaiian lattice' can be recognized by the volcanic soil and rocks that are abundant in the region. Volcanic vegetation can also be seen lining the roads. Note that the angle of the roads is a big clue for the area, and that this lattice was built on the slope of Mauna Loa.

Hilo fits nicely into the coastal Hawai'i landscape (lush and somewhat built up). What makes it unique is the grid format of many of its roads. You can also sometimes see Mauna Kea in the west.

Note by MB: Other grids also exist on Hawaii island (notably Hawaiian Lattice, and the area south of Hilo), but they look very different. Each has their own meta describing them.
Honolulu, located on southern Oʻahu, is by far the largest city and urban area in Hawaii. If you are in a dense urban area and can see tall buildings, you will always be in or near Honolulu.
In most of Hawaii, houses are built on flat plains. If you see Houses on hillsides, you are most likely around the Ko'olau range in eastern Oahu, often in suburbs of Honolulu.
Hualalaei (a large mountain) rises to the east of Kona.

The Island of Hawai’i (also referred to as The Big Island) is both the largest and farthest southeast island with Street View coverage in the state. The interior areas feature rolling, grassy plains and volcanic rocks. You can typically see one or more of the island’s volcanoes from the road.

What sets apart the mountains on this island is that they are more sloping and gradual than on other islands.

The Island of Kauai is the furthest west island in Hawaii with official Google coverage. This island has deep red soil and has large rugged hills with lush, jungle-like vegetation. This island also has exclusively Generation 3 and Smallcam coverage.

NOTE: Other islands such as Maui and Molokaʻi have similar soil colours, but the hillsides on them will typically have less dense vegetation.
The town of Kaunakakai is the largest settlement on the Island of Molokaʻi. It is the only area on the island with an ‘urban’ vibe.

The Island of Lānaʻi is a small, yet distinct island that lies just south of Moloka’i. A volcano is found just east of the centre of the island, adjacent to the town of Lānaʻi. In this area, tall Cook pines are abundant. In addition, some main roads near the centre of the island are lined with younger Cook pines.
West Maui can often see Molokai and/or Lanai to the west. The northern part of the west coast has the West Maui Mountains rising to the east.

cards.a: Hawaii - Landscape - Mauna Loa Observatory Road
cards.note:
This road "looks like Mars", and has large volcanic rocks on its sides.

Note by MB: Unlike the road on Red Hill, this road does not have center lines.

The Island of Molokaʻi is just southeast of the Island of Oʻahu. This island features deep red soil, dry-looking vegetation, and a prominent volcano on the eastern end of the island. Molokaʻi is also very sparsely populated. This island only has Generation 3 and Smallcam coverage.

Note by MB: In the newest smallcam coverage, the island doesn't look as dry as in Gen 3 (due to different season).

The Island of Oʻahu lies southeast of Kauai. It is known for being home to the Honolulu urban area. It also is home to steep, lush hills, which can be commonly seen from all around the island, especially in Honolulu’s suburbs. Generation 4 coverage is common on Oʻahu.

The Red Hill can easily be recognised by this unique barren, rocky landscape. Due to the high altitude, clouds are usually visible below you.

Note by MB: In newer smallcam coverage the hill looks not that red, but the coverage is still recognizable. Also, unlike the Mauna Lea observatory road on Hawai'i, this road has yellow center lines.
The road around and east of Seaview (Hawai'i island) is very distinct, as it combines the volcanic rock landscape with water immediately to the South.
Hawaii island has the only currently active volcano and is the most recently formed island, so lots of volcanic rock is common.

Akureyri is the second-biggest city in Iceland and is located in a North-South oriented valley, along the western edge of the bay. The city features mountains ranges to the east and west, making it recognisable.
The mountains west of Akureyri contain many valleys, sandwiched between tall, often slightly snowcapped peaks. Most of these valleys generally face north to northeast.
The wide valley around Eiðar is slightly hilly and agricultural, with tall, snowy peaks visible in the distance on either side, to the east and northwest, respectively.
The Westfjords region features numerous narrow fjords, surrounded by moderately tall, and mostly flat-topped mountains.
Very foggy coverage can be found around the town of Bakkagerði, in northeastern Iceland. The fog can also be seen from a distance.
The southern coast of Iceland features some impressive glaciers visible from the ring road, spilling into the sea from the Vatnajökull ice cap.

The valley around Hallormsstaður has a distinct northeast/southwest angle with low-lying mountains on either side, a wide river flowing through it, and an unusual amount of trees for Iceland. Some of the sideroads are in the forests.
The Island of Heimaey can easily be recognised by seeing these ragged rocky cliffs overlooking the town of Vestmannaeyjabær. Similar cliffs can be seen on the islands off the coast.

Barren landscapes consisting mostly of dark volcanic gravel, with little to no vegetation or signs of life, are typical of the inland regions of Iceland. Most such covered roads are located in the east.
The far east of the country is also home to several fjords. What distinguishes them from the Westfjords are the generally larger and more jagged mountains.

Reykjavík is the capital and by far the largest city in Iceland. The city is mostly flat with slight hills, and is located on the south side of a bay. It is most recognizable as it is significantly larger than other Icelandic cities, with a large urban area and “bigger city” feel.

NOTE: The city of Akureyri can feel urban in some places. You can distinguish it from Reykjavik as it has mountains to the east and west.
You can recognise the area near the town of Selfoss from its distinct flat-ridge mountain. Due to the otherwise flat landscape, this mountain can be seen from a wide area.

The Southwest agricultural area in Iceland can be identified by its relatively flat farmland landscape scattered with numerous farmsteads, fields, meadows and grasslands.

NOTE: Although there are other smaller agricultural areas in Iceland, mountains in this area tend to be quite distant, making it unique.

This is a volcanic rock, which is recognizable by it's dark color with white mineral patches on it.

It is mostly found between Pune and Jalgaon.

It's important to note that this rock alone, without the mineral patches is more widely spread.

cards.a: India - Landscape - Andhra Pradesh - Red Soil
cards.note:
Andhra Pradesh has a long coast along the bay of Bengal and it is fairly recognizable because of the red soil combined with overall flatness. This is the area in which you fill find red soil in Andhra Pradesh.

Flat landscape with red soil and lots of Palmyra should pretty much always give the eastern India coast.
A rocky desert can be found in this valley southwest of Nandyala, AP.
Hilliness in Assam is found mostly South or East of Nagaon.
If you see Mountains to the North in Assam, you're on the border to Arunachal Pradesh. In my experience, this is a particularly common sight on the border east of Itanagar.

Wind turbines aligned on top of mountain ranges are very common in these mountain ranges valleys I would say. (I know there are some in RJ as well)

Even without wind turbines, you can click in this valley if you have a good north/south angle. I would even say that it is the only place in India with such big N/S dry ranges to the west AND to the east.

Differentiations:

  • Western ghats mountains in Maharashtra (Pune-Nashik area) have different angles
  • The other Mountain Range in Andhra Pradesh (near Odisha border) is less dry.
Chaukhamba, located near the town of Ukhimath, is a mountain massif covered in snow which can be recognised by its three distinct peaks, with the centre peak being the tallest.

Coastal Andhra Pradesh is characterized by a flat, agricultural landscape with coastal bushes

50/50 Tip ! Similar bushes can also be found in Gujarat, but Gujarat will often have distinct holey poles or have a boxy car. Also, Gujarat will primarily have date palms whereas Andhra will have palmyra palms as the main occurrence in palm trees.

The harder rounds in Andhra are the coastal, agricultural ones without any Palmyra or any pole. This basically becomes a 50/50 with any other flat & agricultural state.
Distinctly dark soil is mainly found in Maharashtra and adjacent regions.

Dark soil in India is usually found in and around Maharashtra.

In many cases you can see trident poles together with this dark soil, which will put you in Northern Karnataka, usually near the Maha border (free 4.5k+)

cards.a: India - Landscape - Dry Ganges River Valley
cards.note: Southern Haryana and Southern Uttar Pradesh are very agricultural, but often still look dry. These areas look like a mix of Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh.
In Ladakh and northern Himachal Pradesh you can find an extremely dry landscape with little to no vegetation within the Himalayan mountains.
If you have a Telangana/Andra pole or Telugu with a dry landscape, you are likely in the area between Anantapur, AP and Shadnagar, TG (see image)
Elevated Roads (similar to Bangladesh), with a dry landscape, are common in and around Jharkhand.
While a lot of the coverage in Jammu is located in flat parts, there are some areas north and northeast of the city of Jammu with elevation, where you will be able to see a lot of pines.

The northern plains, also known as the Ganges River Valley, of India are very fertile with extremely flat and open agricultural fields.

Note by MB: Agriculture can be found in many parts of India. I think what sets apart these Northern Plains is the lack of palm trees (except for the occasional date palms and the Palmyra palm spam in Bihar).

Salt flats and coastal marshes with nearly no vegetation, other than short yellow or brown grass, can be found in parts of Gujarat. Shallow bodies of water can often be seen around these areas.

NOTE: The soil in western Rajasthan will be a lot more sandy and you’ll typically be able to see short desert shrubs.

Around Guntur in Andhra Pradesh, you can find a landscape that combines the Andhra Pradesh Panhandle and the agricultural east coast further south.

You will have lots of agriculture (more than in Panhandle) and also many palm trees (more than in the coastal region further south).

cards.a: India - Landscape - Haryana - North Haryana vibes
cards.note:
The northern part of Haryana is very green and agricultural.

Note by MB: Ganges River Valley in general looks like this, but I feel like this area is even greener and lusher, and it also has more sugarcane.

cards.a: India - Landscape - Himachal Pradesh - North/South Valley
cards.note:
The city of Manali is fairly recognizable due to it being one of the two areas with coverage in a recognizable north-south valley. The other is from Kullu to Nagwain 50 km south of it.

The only way I came up with to tell the 2 apart is the vegetation but this is kinda fake since both cities are located in the same valley.

According to me, Manali has poplar trees and pines within the city whereas the other area doesn’t have much of those and mostly consists of random trees.
The by far tallest mountains in India are found in the Himalayas.
Coverage extends to roads that are very high in altitude, so snow can be visible on the end of the streetview east of Leh.
There are a few places where you can have elevation in Madhya Pradesh. The main elevation areas are around Yawal and satpura park, as well as south of Indore

cards.a: India - Landscape - Madhya Pradesh - Red Soil
cards.note: Within Madhya Pradesh, a reddish or pinkish soil is generally more common towards the East.
The landscape west of the Western Ghatts in Maharashtra is quite unique. It has a lot of forests, and a dark brown soil. It's mostly a vibe thing, but it looks kinda like Kerala but with less palms.

The Mechuka valley is the only place in Northeast India where snowy mountains are visible. The valley contains brownish grass and a plethora of Bhutan white pine. North of Mechuka the coverage gradually becomes overcast and somewhat dark.
The landscape in Mizoram mainly consists of lush, green valleys with fairly low vegetation with eroded, smooth hillsides with a flat top.
The landscape in Mizoram mainly consists of lush, green valleys with fairly low vegetation with eroded hillsides having many small peaks scattered around.
Near the southern tip of Tamil Nadu, you can find these large monolithic mountains, with huge exposed rocks. Several of these mountains can be seen from afar, especially the Magenthiragiri hills.

cards.a: India - Landscape - Mountains in Tamil Nadu
cards.note: Mountains in Tamil Nadu can be found along the western border. Additionally, there's a lot of mountains west of Madurai and some east of Salem.

cards.a: India - Landscape - NH3 between Gramphu and Dalang
cards.note: This section of road features huge mountains, with a little bit more **green on their slopes. **

The panhandle of Andhra Pradesh looks quite different than the rest of the state. It is much greener (and has an arguably "darker greener" tone). There are also A LOT more coconut palms here than anywhere else in AP.

Other parts of Andhra Pradesh do have Palmyra Palms, but Coconut palms are kinda rare outside of the panhandle.

The area south of Tirupati in Andhra Pradesh can also look extremely similar, but it has a lot less coverage.
Punjab is generally a very flat state. If you know you're in Punjab, but it's hilly or mountains, you're on the border to Himachal Pradesh
The biggest mountainous areas in Rajasthan are around Alwar max northeast and Udaipur - Mount Abu area
In Rajasthan, there is a North-east angled ridge going from Mount Abu area to New Delhi
In Rajasthan, rolling hills are common for the area south of Udaipur

Rajasthan is a state that is drier than its surrounding states. It's difficult to explain, but many locs in Rajasthan just have a certain 'drier' vibe. If you saw this loc and thought 'This looks like Rajasthan', pat yourself on the back :)
Red soil can be found in several regions, but mainly near the southern west coast and in and around Chhattisgarh and western Odisha.
A pretty straight east-west range with a slight north east angle can be found near Rewa. It is fairly easy to recognize.

Telangana and Andra Pradesh have a lot of “rockiness”. It can be rocks on the side of the road, boulders or even rocky hill slopes but they share that in common.

I found it to be more in Telangana so the meta is here, but note that it can extend to surrounding states of Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh.

Note by MB: In my experience, in AP, rockiness is very common west of the ridge from Tirupati to Nallamala Forest.

Since Imphal is located in a valley, it is fairly simple to recognize it after a few games.

The landscape around the city consists of agricultural fields surrounded by mountains, so it is pretty easy to know you are in Imphal.

cards.a: India - Landscape - Snow Coverage in the Mountains
cards.note:
This coverage can be found on the 3 in Himachal Pradesh near the Ladakh border.

The coverange extends from Zing Zing Bar to Killingsarai

cards.a: India - Landscape - Southern Tamil Nadu Red Soil
cards.note: A flat, bushy landscape with very red soil can be found in southern Tamil Nadu.

The shape of the mountains iin this valley are truly unique : very dry, very high in elevation and sparsely green.

If you have trouble making the difference between this road and the NH3 to the west because it looks roughly similar, just know that the NH3 is paved whilst the Spiti river valley roads usually are not.
The city of Tirupati, AP can easily be recognized by the huge ridge in the North. Other metas, like black&yellow Tuk-Tuks, two-indent poles or simply Telugu language, can help confirm.

cards.a: India - Landscape - Western Ganges River Valley
cards.note: The western Ganges River Valley (Punjab/Haryana/Western UP) usually looks wetter and greener than the general Ganges River Valley. You can often see rice and sugarcane. Note that areas like this can still be found in other parts of the river valley, this is not a 100% meta

The Western Ghats Mountains in the western part of Maharashtra can be recognised by their distinct ridgelines, often having plateaus rather than peaks. The northern part is drier while the southern part has more vegetation.

NOTE: During the rainy season the mountains will turn green and appear quite different.

The western part of Meghalaya basically looks like bangladesh with hills. There are a lot of areca palms, banana trees and palms.

“Hilly forests with areca palms surrounding flat agricultural fields” is how I would best describe this part of Meghalaya.
The western parts of Rajasthan can commonly be recognised by the dry landscape with sandy soil.

The western half of Uttarakhand is typically far more barren than the other Himalayan regions, due to logging and erosion. The coverage northwest of Dehradun on the Himachal Pradesh Border has some especially barren hills full of brown grass and small roads next to cliffs.
The Odisha Hills are very "wonky", i.e. they're undulating and can also very greatly in height.
Unique hilly landscape with dead trees. Note that not all coverage in this park looks like this.

The Nusas typically look drier than other regions in Indonesia. The islands get especially dry towards the east, especially in Generation 3. Vegetation tends to look less tropical, but instead more brown with a lack of leaves. Sumba Island is also the driest of the Nusas.

NOTE: While less common, other regions such as Java can look similarly dry. Make sure to look out for other clues before guessing.
The region around Lake Toba, in North Sumatra, can be recognized by mountains surrounding the lake and Samosir Island in the middle. Overcast coverage is also common for the region.
Palu Bay is a unique slightly north-west facing bay just north of Palu city, which features mountains to the west of the bay, and a flat, more urbanised landscape to the east.
Red soil can often be found on Batam and the Bangka Belitung islands, located east of mainland Sumatra.

This savannah landscape is occasionally seen on North Sumba.

NOTE: In Generation 3, you will always see a white car.

Mount Fuji is the tallest mountain in Japan, with a gradual incline and often snowy summit.

Depending on the elevation, it can be seen from far away. This can create some excellent region guesses, especially if you account for direction and distance.

Japan is notably a very mountainous country. However, there are some regions that are quite flat, being the Nobi and Kanto plains. While at times they can look very similar, determining that it is one or the other can be very helpful.

NOTE: While there are, of course, other flat areas in Japan, these two are the most recognizable.
Road 35 is surrounded by hills and mountains, and the ground is mostly covered in green shrubs. Curved lamp posts are posted at regular intervals on the northeastern side of the road.
Most of Road 45 south of Mudayy is unpaved and goes generally north to south, through some very rough hilly terrain. The soil is light and very rocky. Beware that the southernmost stretch is paved.

Just north of Adam, you’ll find a flat desert landscape with greyish soil and mountains in the distance, notably one long ridge to the south followed by two smaller and rounder hills to the east and southeast. Other mountains are also visible to the north and west.
If you are surrounded by mountains on all sides, and you are in a somewhat urban area, you are likely just southeast of Muscat, in Al Amarat.

South of Bidiyah you can find a couple of dirt roads going through a slightly rolling landscape consisting of orange-pink sand and small yellow-ish shrubs. The roads mainly go between long and low sand dunes with a general south-south-west direction.
Sandy desert with light coloured green and yellow shrubs can be found in northeastern Oman, mainly south and west of Bidiyah.
Coastal Road 41 features one of the sandiest landscapes in Oman, with very light sand all around. The coast is sometimes visible in the distance.

Coastal Road 41 features one of the sandiest landscapes in Oman, with very light sand all around. The coast is sometimes visible in the distance. On the north-to-south stretch, you can see a distant ridge to the west.
Northern Oman features a dry mountainous landscape similar to eastern UAE. The south coast of Oman also rarely features some similar mountains.
Masirah Island features a dry and slightly hilly landscape, typically with somewhat grey soil and with brown shrubs visible. The front camera on the island is slightly smudged.

Masirah Island features a dry and slightly hilly landscape, typically with somewhat grey soil and with brown shrubs visible. Road 51, which circulates the island, usually only has a white centre road line, which can help in recognising it. The front camera on the island is slightly smudged.
Most of Road 45 south of Mudayy is unpaved and goes generally north to south, through some very rough hilly terrain. The soil is light and very rocky. Beware that the southernmost stretch is paved.

Most of the coverage in the Musandam Governorate exclave is coastal, with rocky cliffs usually hugging the road. A majority, but not all, of this coverage will have the coast to the west, excluding any other roads in the country with a similar look.
Going further north, Road 32 travels through a hilly desert landscape, in a general northern direction.

The mountains north of Nizwa have an amount of green bushes that are unusually large for the north. The mountains are very rocky and jagged, which differentiates them from the more rolling mountains in the south.

cards.a: Landscape - North of Al Awaya Road
cards.note: The road north of Al Awaya features a desert landscape with dark grey soil, which is not common in the south. The road itself still has the orange tint characteristic of southwest Oman.

cards.a: Landscape - North of Al Mazyunah Road
cards.note: The unpaved road north of Al Mazyunah, near the Yemen border, has a north-north-west bound angle, and the desert has sandy, red-tinted sand, which still has some shrubbery around. You can see some hills in the distance. The southwards driving direction and sunny weather can be used as confirmation.

A road going through large orange-pink sand dunes can be found north of Fasad.

NOTE: The same dunes can be seen in the distance close to the northern part of the Yemen border.
This road leading from the 65 to the town of Orocue is characterized by its unique angle and the orange/brown dirt.
Close to the southern coast, especially around Salalah, you will find a rolling hills landscape. The area commonly features rocky ground, bushes and small trees as well as some fairly green valleys.
Road 42/49 east of Salalah is a scenic coastal road that features a lot of light-coloured tall rocky cliffs. The coast is also often visible.
Salalah is located on a flat coastal plain with rolling mountains surrounding it to the north.
Around the town of Ubar, you can find patches of green agricultural land surrounded by desert.
The western stretch of Road 41 has wide shoulders similar to Road 31, however, the more northwest-bound angle along with the reddish soil should tell them apart.

Crossing into the Ash Sharqiyah North Governorate, the shoulders become wide, like those on Road 31. However, unlike Road 31, the desert here is darker and has more shrubs and greenery. A long portion of the road also has overcast coverage. The lighter red section is no longer road 32 but still features the wide shoulders. The landscape further north also gets hillier and more vegetated.
Cerro del Bernal is a distinct extinct volcano that is found in southern Tamaulipas. It can be found heading directly northwest of Tampico or west of Morón.
The outskirts of Ciudad Juárez features a lot of dirt roads with a distinct shade of orange soil and low shrubs.
The area around Ciudad Obregon is distinct due to the pinkish-tan soil and canals found around the city’s agricultural areas.

The town of Guaymas has a lot of jagged cliffs and mountains that make the area very distinct. The soil is also distinctly pinkish and organ-pipe cacti can be seen scattered on the hills and next to the road.

This tall, flat ridge, with very prominent ridgelines, belongs to the Maderas del Carmen Biosphere Reserve in Northern Coahuila near the US border.

NOTE: The only road the mountain range can be observed from is the Federal Highway 53 that leads to Boquillas del Carmen.

The 40D that crosses the Sinaloa-Durango state line is recognizable by the stunning lush cliffs and mountains along the road. The highway commonly passes through tunnels and the road itself features double yellow middle roadlines.

The 54 is a divided highway that runs through northeastern Zacatecas which features yucca trees spammed on both sides of the road. Additionally, the streetview car is often exposed and appears almost white due to the sunlight.
The area around Mexicali features flat farmland with a ridge to the west. Washingtonia palms are very common and these poles made out of brown wood can be found.
The Monterrey metropolitan area features tall stunning mountain ranges that surround the city.

cards.a: Mexico - Landscape - Morelos Prickly Pear Farms
cards.note: Farms of prickly pear are commonly found in north east Morelos, where they foreground **striking, sculpturally eroded dry hills. **
These reddish brown-tinged hills, often accompanied by large boulders, are a common sight for the northern half of Baja California.
The town of Los Coloradas is famously known for the pink lakes around the area.

The area around San Cristóbal Suchixtlahuaca and south of it in Oaxaca often feature rolling hills with really distinct orange and beige-tinged soil, passing from one colour to the other with each hill. The beige-tinged soil can be seen more prominent in some locations.

cards.a: Mexico - Landscape - Sierra del Abra Tanchipa
cards.note: This extremely long and flat ridge is found in the Sierra del Abra Tanchipa Biosphere Reserve in eastern San Luis Potosi.

The twin volcanoes of Iztaccíhuatl and Popocatépetl are found on the border between the State of Mexico and Puebla. Keep in mind that they are usually much less visible than depicted in the image, which is just for reference.

The western parts of Chihuahua and Durango can feature a rocky mountainous landscape covered with pine forests. In general, these pines are shorter and more stunted in appearance than pine forests of the central or south.

Almost blindingly white soil in the Yucatan peninsula is most common in Quintana Roo.

NOTE: This is only consistent in Generation 3.

The 82 on the island of Andoya, which is part of the Lofoten archipelago, is flat apart from one tabletop looking hill. In generall, the hills on this road are quite unique and recognizable. You will find short scrubs along the road. Often, you will be able to see water.

This road uses dark rocks as bridges. You will see water on both sides of the road. The coverage features dark clouds.

The road includes the famous Storseisundet bridge.
While fjords can be found along most of the Norwegian coast, deep fjords surrounded by tall mountains are most common between Bergen and Trondheim.

This road features huge mountains. It is a skinny road that has water to the east. Lots of sections have bridges or open tunnels. You will frequently find fireweed on the sides of the road. The vegetation on this road has a yellowish tone.

cards.a: Norway - Landscape - E10 on the border of Troms and Nordland
cards.note: This road runs through a valley. You can see a big mountain range along the road, with no trees on the mountain. Some sections are very green, and some section feature fireweed.

cards.a: Norway - Landscape - E10, East of Narvik
cards.note: This road is very green and usually features big mountains with no trees. Right on the Swedish border you will find parts without trees.

cards.a: Norway - Landscape - End of the World Road
cards.note: This famous road can be identified by the lack of trees and the small white rocks. The visibility in the coverage is somewhat low. Some sections are very flat, while others can have small hills and lakes.
Exposed rock, often spotted with small coastal pines and bushes, is mainly found on the south coast.
Barren highlands, with no trees or bushes, and often with rocky mountains along the road, are mostly found in the southwest.
Distinct, sharp, rocky mountains with few trees can be seen on the Lofoten Archipelago.
Lysevegen is a very windy and skinny road with 28 180° turns down the mountain. Notably, there are big power lines visible. You can see huge mountains in the distance. The coverage is very cloudy.
The northeast of Norway can typically be recognized by a somewhat rolling landscape, rather than tall mountains, and vegetation mainly consisting of very small birches combined with patched grass.
Coastal grasslands with little to no other vegetation and only somewhat low, distant mountains can be found by coastal roads in the far north.

The largest concentration of farmland is found in the southeast, in the general vicinity of Oslo. The area is much flatter than most of the country, and it is common to get a rolling landscape with smooth, round forested hills in the distance. The area southeast of Oslo is particularly flat.
This island has only Gen 2 coverage. You will see lots of boats everywhere. The landscape is flat and islandish (duh).

Along the Russian border you can see this noticeably humid and green-looking road, with very overcast and occasionally foggy coverage. The trees are somewhat low and mainly consist of thin birches and pines.

The farmland south of Stavanger is flatter than most of the country. The fields look vast and open, and it is very common to see rock walls made of large, round rocks. Furthermore, rather than crops, most fields will only contain grass.

Trollstigen leads down a huge mountain, and is surrounded by such. The road is very steep and windy. The rock is very dark and has green moss on it. Some sections are cut into the rock, with waterfalls appearing.
The farmlands surrounding Trondheim are generally very hilly, and the hills are typically both steeper and more uneven than in the southeast.

The 1N near the Piura and Lambayeque border has a distinct looking landscape. It features a semidesert landscape and has overcast coverage in Generation 3. The new Generation 4 is drier but still looks somewhat similar.

The 1S south of the city of Ica is not divided and mostly follows the coast. The soil is often red or orange in these areas, and there is little-to-no vegetation. This road is also entirely covered with the Generation 4 camera.

Ruta 28B between the towns of Kimbiri and Echarate is a paved road with very faded or missing road lines. It is also characterised by being a relatively small road with Generation 4 coverage, which hugs the hillside and is located next to a river valley.

Ruta 30C in eastern Peru uses a white Street View car in Generation 3 between the cities of Planchon and Iñapari. It features dense forest, few villages, and resembles interior areas of Brazil. Some of this area has been overwritten with Generation 4. Most of this segment runs north to south.
Ruta 5N between the towns of San Alejandro and Esperanza is a relatively straight, flat road in good condition. This road primarily runs north-south through the rainforest.

Areas near the cities of Ica, Arequipa, and Tacna feature barren and mostly flat desert landscapes that can resemble areas of northern Chile. You can typically see mountains in the distance, primarily while looking to the east.

The southern city of Cusco is recognizable by its prevalence of both red brick and Spanish colonial style buildings. Cusco is surrounded by mountains on all sides and features an airport in the middle of the city. Due to its proximity and similar architecture, Cusco superficially resembles the Bolivian city of La Paz.

In higher elevation areas near the centre of the country, exposed rocky outcroppings are commonly seen in the sides of hills and mountains. Some areas with the highest concentrations are near Lago Chinchaycocha (Junin District) stretching south towards the city of Ayacucho.

NOTE: Exposed rocks can rarely be seen anywhere in the country, so use this meta with some caution.

cards.a: Peru - Landscape - Flat Landscape between Mountains
cards.note:
A flat landscape in the mountains of Peru is usually seen in central Puno and around Lake Chinchaycocha.

NOTE: This landscape might look similar to Bolivia. Make sure to look out for other clues before guessing.

Iquitos is a city in northeast Peru. It is an isolated city with only Generation 3 Street View coverage. Three-wheeled tuk-tuks, overcast skies, and rolling Amazonian landscapes are commonly seen in the area. This coverage is isolated from other areas of northern Peru.
The road to Iquitos can be recognized by black car Gen 3, lack of center lines and rolling Amazonian landscape

The valley connecting the cities of Jauja and Huancayo features a flat plain with plentiful trees, agricultural areas, and small villages. North-south oriented mountains can be seen on both edges of the valley.

North of the city of Huancayo lies a shallow lake called Lake Chinchaycocha (also referred to as ‘the middle lake.’). This lake is generally marshy and a range of mountains can be seen to the east of the lake. This lake can look similar to Lake Titicaca, but is generally less densely populated and features fewer trees.
Patches of light green lichen can be seen covering rocks and growing on the ground in high elevation areas of central and southern Peru.

cards.a: Peru - Landscape - North of Titicaca Wetness
cards.note: The coverage on the north side of Lake Titicaca was taken during a significantly wetter season than the coverage taken on the south side of Lake Titicaca.
The areas adjacent to the northern Amazonian city of Tarapoto feature moderately tall foliage-covered mountains and can bear a similar resemblance to the hilly areas of Colombia or Brazil.

The landscape northwest of the city of Piura is generally dry, featuring a low amount of vegetation with a few shrubs and bushes. The landscape is hilly, which distinguishes it from other Piura regions.

Dark red-tinted soil is found in several areas of Peru. Some notable areas include the areas near Cusco and Ayacucho in the south of the country, as well as areas near the northern cities of Cajamarca and Tarapoto. It can be found to a lesser extent in adjacent regions.

Coastal agricultural valleys in the middle and south are commonly sandwiched between dry mountains with no vegetation. The general orientation of these valleys are southwest-northeast.

NOTE: Agricultural valleys in the north of Peru can look similar, but often feature more shrubs and trees on the mountains.

Similarly, taller mountains near the middle of the country often feature rocky and sharp mountain tops. The main region of these mountains stretches from near the city of Huaraz southward to the city of Cusco; generally away from the coast.
Far north Peru features mountains that are often covered in shrubby trees and bushes. Closer to the coast and the Ecuador border, these mountains are often quite dry in appearance.
The southwestern landscape of Piura is generally dry, featuring a low amount of vegetation with a few shrubs and bushes. The landscape is mostly flat, but you will sometimes see rolling hills.
The city of Tacna in the far south of Peru has this distinct dry ridge to the north.
Low grass, a few hills, stone walls in villages and brown brick buildings are typical for the region south of Lake Titicaca in eastern Peru.

These three landscapes are typically found along offroads in Tumbes. You will always see sandy soil with either green or withered bushes.

NOTE: In addition, Tumbes does not have black cars on off roads. Make sure to consider it whenever you see such landscapes with a white Street View car.

Volcanoes are often seen in and around the city of Arequipa.

NOTE: Within Peru, volcanoes are only found in the southeast in the highlighted area.
The Arayat Volcano can be recognised by being completely surrounded by flat agricultural fields.
On central Bohol you can find these distinct round grassy hills. The hills generally have dark brown soil beneath the grass, earning them the name of Chocolate Hills.
The Mayon Volcano is one of the tallest mountains in the Philippines and can be recognised by its almost perfect smooth cone shape. Beware that it will very often be covered in clouds.

The forested mountain range in Northern Luzon is characterised by somewhat dry mountainsides and an abundance of pine trees. You may rarely come across a similar landscape on high-altitude roads in Mindanao.

cards.a: South Africa - Landscape - Cape Town Mountains
cards.note: The distinct Table Mountain, located west of Cape Town, can be recognized by its prominent three-kilometre plateau. It is flanked by Devil’s Peak, which is more pyramidal.
Mountains in the Witfontein Nature Reserve, likely George’s Peak, will be visible north from the city of George.

cards.a: South Africa - Landscape - Kruger National Park
cards.note:
The landscape around Kruger National Park is generally flat, with a savannah climate and dry vegetation. You will not see any agriculture and the vegetation is mostly made up of grasses, with small trees dotting the landscape. Red soil can also be seen below the grass.

NOTE: Within the coverage of the park, you will mostly find unpaved gravel roads or small and paved roads without road lines.

cards.a: South Africa - Landscape - Northeastern Dry Season
cards.note:
The northeast of the country can look very dry and somewhat barren, with a lot of orange or red soil. You will often see hills or mountains covered in shrubs.

NOTE: Depending on the season, the coverage can change drastically from dry to very green.

A dry landscape with red soil is typically found in the Northern Cape.

NOTE: This map is a useful guide in guessing based on the climate of South Africa.

cards.a: South Africa - Landscape - R360 North of Bokspits
cards.note:
The section of the R360 north of Bokspits, next to the Botswana border, has asphalt with a recognizable reddish tint. The landscape is arid and features dry greyish trees, shrubs and long golden grass. The road runs in a general north to south direction.

NOTE: Asphalt with a reddish tint can be found on other roads and the southern part of the R360. However, the landscape north of Bokspits looks predominantly like this.

Unique rocky, treeless mountains can be seen in Western Cape, with most of the mountains having tall, steep sides and sharp peaks.

NOTE: Similar mountains can be seen in and around Lesotho.
Grassy rolling hills are generally located in the coastal area of Western Cape between Cape Town and George, and just north of Cape Town. Tall ridges are usually visible to the north or east.

cards.a: South Africa - Landscape - South of Mozambique
cards.note: The landscape near the Mozambique border in the highlighted area is noticeably flat, with green subtropical vegetation.
River valleys surrounded by steep, barren and rocky cliff sides can be found between the cities of Erzurum and Artvin and in the southeast near the city of Hakkâri.
Göreme, west of Kayseri, can be recognised by the tall sandstone monoliths with ancient dwellings carved into them.

In the northeast you will find uncultivated grasslands in valleys surrounded by round hills. Trees are very limited in the region. In Generation 3 the area has an extremely distinct look, with deep green grass covering the hills. It is significantly more difficult to recognise in Generation 4, where the grass has a more arid look.

Along the western shore of Lake Beyşehir and Lake Eğirdir you can find this small single lane road with jagged, exposed rock and Turkish pines to the west. These two can be differentiated by the road west of Lake Eğirdir having a middle road line.

Along the western shore of Lake Beyşehir and Lake Eğirdir you can find this small single lane road with jagged, exposed rock and Turkish pines to the west. These two can be differentiated by the road west of Lake Eğirdir having a middle road line.
Lake Van is by far the biggest lake in Turkey and has a semi-arid landscape, being surrounded by dry grassy hills and occasional trees and agricultural fields near the shore.
Northern Turkey tends to be significantly lusher and more forested than the rest of the country.

Mount Ararat, labelled as Ağrı Dağı on Google Maps, is a dormant volcano in far eastern Turkey and the tallest mountain in the country. It is often seen together with Küçük Ağrı, a smaller volcano to the southeast.
Dark, volcanic rocks are commonly found between the cities of Şanlıurfa and Diyarbakır.
Tennessee and Kentucky look like a mix of Appalachian and Southern Landscape.

The Appalachian mountain range is a low mountain range that runs through the eastern states. The general landscape consists of low, forested mountains, with beech and oak trees being a common sight.

NOTE: Houses in the south generally have less storeys. New England architecture, commonly consisting of wood panelling, high roofs and a porch, is also more common toward the north, especially in New England.
Badlands National Park features these distinct, sand-brown, eroded rock formations. The formations may sometimes appear more rounded, and lighter in colour.

cards.a: United States - Landscape - Big Bend National Park
cards.note: Big Bend National Park is located along the Mexico border in Southwest Texas. It can be identified by its dry, rocky peaks and shrubby foliage. This park is adjacent to the Chihauhan desert, so plants such as yucca and prickly pear cactus are common.

The Black Hills, located in far Western South Dakota and far Eastern Wyoming, are a series of moderately tall mountains with large amounts of conifer trees and rocky outcroppings. The surrounding areas are typically much flatter with lesser tree cover.

NOTE: This area has a similar appearance to many areas within the Rocky Mountains, which lie further to the West.
Landscapes vary quite a bit in New England. Maine in particular can look a lot like Canada.

In the Appalachian area stretching from southern New York to southern Virginia, there are a lot of forest-covered rolling hills, with flat valleys dividing them. A majority of the ridges are oriented Southwest to Northeast.
The soil gets a little more sandy in Central Florida. There are also more pine trees than palms (they’re occasionally seen too).

Central Valley, California can be recognized by its Mediterranean climate. This is reflected in its agriculture, seen in the vineyards and olive trees that can commonly be found here.

In addition, rolling hills can be seen toward the edges of the valley.
Small circular shallow lakes are especially common in Central Florida around Lakeland and Orlando.

Central Colorado is home to a large North-to-South oriented mountain ridge. This divides the Rocky Mountains to the west and the Great Plains to the east.These mountains are adjacent to the major metropolitan areas of Boulder, Denver, and Colorado Springs.

Death Valley National Park can be easily recognized by the dry, sandy, treeless mountains that can be seen from the roads that go through the park. In Generation 3 coverage, the sky can look particularly dusty.

NOTE: Many smaller roads in Death Valley only have Generation 1 coverage.

In far Northeastern Wyoming lies Devil’s Tower, which is a very tall, standalone butte protruding from the surrounding land. This can sometimes be seen from many miles away because of the lack of nearby mountains.
The driftless area in Southwestern Wisconsin is quite unique. It has features of Midwestern States (for example agriculture), but is very hilly.

Deep South Florida, between the metropolitan areas of Ft. Myers and Miami, features dense, jungle-like forests that have few inhabitants. Roads through these areas are commonly very straight and long.

Deep South Florida, between the metropolitan areas of Ft. Myers and Miami, features dense, jungle-like forests that have few inhabitants. Roads through these areas are commonly very straight and long.

The Florida Keys are an archipelago of tropical islands west of Miami. The highway connecting the islands can be recognized by green, tropical vegetation on the sides of the usually single lane road. The soil is also sandy white.

Urban locations are also similar, but with many more planted palm trees and mowed grass being a common sight.

cards.a: United States - Landscape - Glacier National Park
cards.note:
Along the Canadian border in Montana lies Glacier National Park. It is easily recognizable by its extremely tall and steep mountain peaks. Most coverage is also hazy and taken during summer.

NOTE: Other National Parks within the Rocky Mountain range of the US can have a similar appearance, so consider other clues before guessing.

The Great Basin, centred around Nevada, can be recognized by the tall, sometimes snow-capped mountains in the background. There are dry, but grassy, and slightly shrubby plains leading up to the mountains.

cards.a: United States - Landscape - Great Basin - Green
cards.note: Within the Great Basin, greener mountains can be seen in Idaho and central Utah.

cards.a: United States - Landscape - Great Basin - Oregon
cards.note: Within the Great Basin, more gradual, rocky hills can be seen in Oregon.
