The Great Plains are in the middle of the United States and stretch from the Canadian border in the North, to central Texas in the South. This area is primarily flat with few trees. Some areas feature agriculture fields, while others feature dry and barren grassy fields.
In adjacent areas of New Mexico and Texas, smaller foothills of the Guadaloupe Mountains can be seen with relatively flat tops and shrubby foliage.

Along the New Mexico and or Texas border there is a ridge of tall, dry peaks known as the Guadalupe Mountains. In adjacent areas of both states, smaller foothills of these mountains can be seen with relatively flat tops and shrubby foliage.
Flat and marshy landscapes are a common sight in Louisiana.

cards.a: United States - Landscape - Lush Spruce Forest
cards.note: Spruce and pine forests are a common sight in the western United States in New Mexico, Colorado, Wyoming, Montana, and to the west of those states. The lush spruce forest types shown become increasingly common near the Pacific coast in Washington, Oregon, and California.
Some locations in the Mid-Atlantic region can look deceivingly Midwestern but with more trees.
Upstate New York and Pennsylvania are quite forested. Rolling hills are also common.

cards.a: United States - Landscape - Mississippi River Valley
cards.note: The Lower Mississippi River Valley is a very flat and open landscape with red soil in areas of Tennessee, Arkansas, Mississippi, and Northeast Louisiana. Corn and other crops are common in this area.
The Nebraska Sandhills are a recognizable region of rolling hills covered with prairie grass in the central-north part of the state.

Landscapes vary quite a bit in New England. Maine in particular can look a lot like Canada if you know your countries in GeoGuessr. The topography of New England is mostly rolling hills. The forests are littered with fir trees and aspens.
One thing that sets NoCal apart from SoCal is the amount of palm trees. You generally see palms everywhere in the LA area but hardly any in the San Francisco Bay Area.
North Florida has sandier soil and rarely has any palm trees. Most forests are pine forests and the vibes feel more like Florida’s neighbors to the north than Florida itself.
Southwestern Oklahoma features a small area of rocky, shrubby peaks. Some of the mountains are also covered in trees, and the rocks can have a pinkish red tint to them.

The Ouachita Mountains stretch from Eastern Oklahoma into West-Central Arkansas. Unlike the nearby Ozark Mountains, these mountains are typically more steep in nature and easier to see from a distance.

Temperate rainforests are found in coastal areas of Washington, Oregon, and Northern California. These rainforests feature many broadleaf trees, large conifers, and ferns.

NOTE: These rainforests stretch north into coastal British Columbia and Southeast Alaska as well.

cards.a: United States - Landscape - Pine Forest Hills
cards.note: Spruce and pine forests are a common sight in the western United States in New Mexico, Colorado, Wyoming, Montana, and to the west of those states. The landscape that you can see in the picture meanwhile can be found in the states of Colorado, Montana, Wyoming, Utah, New Mexico, Arizona, Idaho, some locations in Nevada, and the eastern portions of Oregon, Washington, and California.

The area spanning from the Montana Border with Saskatchewan to the Western Great Lakes features many ‘prairie potholes.’ These are areas of low-lying wetlands that feature marshy grasses and small, shallow ponds.

You’ll find red soil everywhere in the South. The area where red soil can be found stretches all the way from some parts of Louisiana and Arkansas all the way to southern Virginia through Mississippi, southern Tennessee, Alabama, Georgia, South Carolina, and North Carolina.

The Oklahoma City region in Oklahoma is also notable for its red soil.

cards.a: United States - Landscape - Rio Grande Valley
cards.note: The Rio Grande Valley in South Texas is extremely flat and features shrubby trees and agricultural fields. This area borders the Mexican state of Tamaulipas.

The area stretching from the Canadian border to Northern New Mexico is home to the Rocky Mountains. These jagged, rocky formations often feature many pine trees and visible snow all-year round at the highest peaks. Some areas of the Rocky Mountain Range are noticeably dry, with few trees.

cards.a: United States - Landscape - Rolling Hills in Florida
cards.note: The area between the cities of Orlando and Lakeland in Florida sometimes feature low, rolling hills. Lakes and agricultural fields are also common in this area. This is the only main hilly area in central or southern Florida.

cards.a: United States - Landscape - Roosevelt National Park
cards.note:
Theodore Roosevelt National Park features similar, sand-brown, eroded rock formations to Badlands National Park. The rock formations in this park tend to have more trees on them. Additionally, almost all coverage has fall colours visible.

NOTE: Similar formations can be seen in far eastern Montana as well.

cards.a: United States - Landscape - Rural New Jersey
cards.note: Rural New Jersey looks strikingly southern.

Shiprock is a rock formation and a municipality in northwestern New Mexico. This striking, isolated mountain is visible from distances of up to 40 km (roughly the red square) and is therefore a good clue for identifying the region within the Navajo Nation. Similar rock formations can be seen around Shiprock, but they do not have a long, low stone wall next to them.
South Florida is marshy and tropical. You’ll see an abundance of palm trees here.

cards.a: United States - Landscape - Southern California - Rural
cards.note: Southern California outside the major cities of Los Angeles and San Diego is a barren desert.

cards.a: United States - Landscape - Southern California - Urban
cards.note: In general Los Angeles and San Diego feel more tropical and the houses are more spread out as opposed to the more compact and dense feel of San Francisco.
Spruce and pine forests are a common sight in the western United States in New Mexico, Colorado, Wyoming, Montana, and to the west of those states.

The Southwest, centred around the Four Corners region of Utah, Arizona, New Mexico, and Colorado, feature many mesas and tablelands. Often, these rock formations will be red in colour. Additionally, red soil is common in these areas.

Just west of the metropolitan areas of Austin and San Antonio Texas lies a large area of dry, rocky hills featuring many yucca and prickly pear plants. Texas Live Oak trees are the predominant tree type in this area.
